# generator-shortcuts — exact canonical-fit counterexample

**Question.** For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival
rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it
disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your
proposed generator emits such cases.

## Rival and why it survives the canonical evidence

Among the competitors tested, the strongest canonical-consistent rival is:
**join the paths correctly, then translate the entire packed chain left until
its first colored column is zero.** This differs only in its treatment of the
first object's left margin. All canonical examples checked already start at
column zero, so they cannot distinguish the two rules. The executable
`left_justify_packed_chain` matches all 10 ledger entries tested, comprising two
records with five labeled pairs each; this is not 10 independent puzzle tasks.

Grouping by color and horizontal-only compaction are other useful contrasts, but
are not claimed to fit all canonical examples. No finite sample establishes that
this is the strongest rival in every possible program language; “strongest” here
means the least additional deviation among the explicit rivals actually checked.

## Exact emitted input

Zero is background; each line is one row, with one digit per cell. This is 3x11:

```text
00000000011
09990110010
00000010110
```

It is emitted by the final generator with:

```python
generate(17, 1, grid_h=3, grid_w=11, n_paths=3,
         n_distinct_colors=2, gap=1, anchor_col=1)
```

The actual canonical Racket output is 3x9:

```text
000000011
099911010
000001110
```

The rival instead returns 3x8:

```text
00000011
99911010
00001110
```

The intended result retains the blank first column, since the first path remains
fixed. The rival removes it. The input also contains two disconnected color-1
paths; they must remain distinct objects during extraction.

## Verification and generation coverage

`workspace/adversarial_audits.py` generated the exact input, recorded a clean
self-check, executed the canonical Racket authority, evaluated the explicit rival,
and saved both outputs in `checks/adversarial-audits.json` under
`assigned_shortcut`. The independent geometry implementation agrees with the
Racket output; the dedicated regression compares the rival to that implementation.
The final semantic battery independently links the positive-anchor witness to the
same executable rival and reports a green result.

Reproduce from the packet root, after applying the patch:

```bash
export RACKET_PATH="$PWD/.review/racket-runtime/racket/bin/racket"
python3 repo/generators/664a918eb273/workspace/adversarial_audits.py \
  --repo-root repo --out checks/shortcut-recheck.json
```

Yes, the generator emits this class without overrides as well: 150 of 300 default
draws in the retained census refute this rival. Expanded odd-index defaults keep a
positive first margin; core even-index defaults preserve canonical-like zero
margins. The particular grid above is an exact override replay, not a claim that
this exact grid appeared in the 300-default-draw census. Individual three-example
lessons are not asserted to cover every witness, and hidden solve answers were
not inspected to establish this finding.
